comments.author: @davidcarmack5074
comments.text: Hawaii is not the most remote Islands. Try Tristan de Cuna.

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: Thanks for pointing that out! Tristan da Cunha is indeed one of the most isolated inhabited island groups in the world. Hawaii is often described as the most isolated major population center on Earth, but that doesn't mean it's the most remote island group. We appreciate the clarification, and Tristan da Cunha would certainly be a fascinating destination for a future documentary!

comments.author: @TravelUnknown-1602
comments.text: Hawaii makes you realize that isolation can be both beautiful and limiting. You’re surrounded by incredible nature, but the ocean also separates you from almost everything else. Would that feel peaceful to you—or claustrophobic?

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: That's such an interesting way to look at Hawaii. I think the same isolation that gives the islands their sense of peace can also be one of the biggest challenges of living there. For some people, the ocean feels like freedom; for others, it may feel like a boundary. That's part of what makes island life so fascinating. Thanks for sharing this perspective!

comments.author: @Worldtravel_100
comments.text: The people of Hawaii embody a profound respect for nature and a strong sense of community (Ohana). They live in harmony with their unique environment, valuing humility, resilience, and tradition over modern distractions. Their connection to the land and each other turns the islands into more than just a destination—it makes them a true home.

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: Beautifully said. That sense of connection—to the land, to family, and to community—is one of the most meaningful things we wanted to explore in this video. Hawaii is certainly known for its extraordinary beauty, but understanding the people and their relationship with the islands gives that beauty a much deeper meaning. Thank you for sharing such a thoughtful reflection!

comments.author: @rhondareimers5361
comments.text: I’m 72 and have lived in Hawaii since I was 18. It’s expensive, but manageable. There’s no way I would choose to live anywhere else.  It’s a beautiful culture which I have enormous respect for.  And the rain, rainbows and trade winds outweigh the hurricanes , tsunami warnings and volcanic eruptions!  Sending all Aloha 🌈🌋🌴

replies.author: @ExploreTravelDocs
replies.text: Living in Hawaii since you were 18 and still saying, at 72, that you wouldn’t choose anywhere else—that really says more than any travel brochure ever could. ❤🌺 After more than 50 years, Hawaii clearly became much more than a beautiful place to live—it became home. I love how you acknowledge the hurricanes, tsunami warnings and eruptions, yet still talk about the rain, rainbows, trade winds and culture with so much affection. Sending Aloha right back to you! 🌈🌴❤
